releases.notes:
## 1.0.3
### Added
- **A medicine cabinet, and the apothecary who works at it.** The block is a job site and nothing else: three planks over three glass bottles over three planks makes a cabinet that faces the player who placed it, and from that one property everything else follows. A villager standing near an unclaimed cabinet takes the **apothecary** profession and opens five levels of trade - licorice and coptis potions at level one, seaweed iodized salt and salt powder at level two, a glucose meter and test strips at level three, mandrake fruit and gymnopilus at level four, ephedrine and grapefruit juice at level five - two offers per level, twelve uses each, at the same emerald prices and experience values the vanilla professions use. Every item on the list already existed; the cabinet is what turns the pharmacy's stock into something a village can sell.
  - **The trades are datapack entries, because 26.3 moved the whole trade system out of code.** `VillagerTrade` and `TradeSet` are registry types now, loaded from `data/<namespace>/villager_trade/<profession>/<level>/<name>.json` and `data/<namespace>/trade_set/<profession>/level_<n>.json`, and the Fabric API's `TradeOfferHelper` - the obvious place to have hooked this - does not exist in the resolved jar at all. So the mod ships ten trades, five trade sets and five tags as JSON, and the only Kotlin is the profession, the point of interest and the block. That split is not a preference: there is no code path left to register a trade from Java or Kotlin.
  - **A trade's registry id is its path *including* the file name**, which is the one detail that cost a build. The tags initially listed `aliment:apothecary/1/coptis_potion`, reading the level directory as the id; the real id is `aliment:apothecary/1/emerald_coptis_potion`, because the file is named for its cost and its result, the way vanilla's `emerald_ender_pearl` is. A tag naming an id that does not exist is a hard failure - the server refuses to start with *Unbound values in registry minecraft:villager_trade* - which is the good version of this mistake. The bad version is the reverse: had the tags been right and the files wrong, the villager would simply have stood there offering a level with nothing in it.
  - **The point of interest had to join `minecraft:acquirable_job_site`, and nothing in the profession object says so.** Declaring the job site on the profession is only half of it: an *unemployed* villager has the profession `minecraft:none`, whose `acquirableJobSite` predicate tests membership in that tag and nothing else, so it is the tag, not the profession, that decides whether the cabinet is ever walked to. Vanilla's own thirteen job sites are in it for the same reason. The mod's `aliment:medicine_cabinet` is added alongside them and the tag merges, so no vanilla entry is displaced.
  - **The work sound is the cleric's**, there being no apothecary one: `SoundEvents` carries work sounds for the thirteen vanilla professions only, and `VILLAGER_WORK_CLERIC` is the one that means *standing at a block mixing something*. A silent workstation would have been the only alternative.

releases.notes:
## 1.0.2

### Added
- Add the **grapefruit tree** and the fruit that hangs under it:
  - `aliment:grapefruit_log`, `aliment:grapefruit_leaves` and `aliment:grapefruit_sapling` are a small citrus of its own. It generates in the jungles and the savannas at one attempt per six chunks, and a sapling grows the same tree.
  - `aliment:grapefruit` is the fruit, and it hangs: vanilla's `minecraft:attached_to_leaves` decorator puts it in the block directly under a canopy leaf, and it can only exist while there is still a leaf or a log above it, so breaking the canopy drops it.
  - One grapefruit crafts into **eight** `aliment:grapefruit_slice`, which is the part a player eats: **2 hunger**, **3 saturation points**, **5 water**, **1 naringin** and **10 vitamin C** - the vitamin C being what a carrot is worth, because a slice is a plant food and a citrus besides. It is the only food in the mod that also drinks, and one of the few that can be eaten on a full stomach, because a player eats it for the naringin rather than for the hunger.
- Add the **grapefruit wood set**, a full second wood alongside the willow's: `grapefruit_wood`, `stripped_grapefruit_log`, `stripped_grapefruit_wood`, planks, stairs, slab, fence, fence gate, door, trapdoor, pressure plate, button, shelf, standing and hanging signs, a potted sapling, and its own **boat and boat with chest** - each with its own entity type, model layers and textures, as every wood's boat now needs. Its own `aliment:grapefruit_logs` tag is what its recipes take, so a plank recipe cannot be satisfied with willow logs, and it joins the vanilla `planks`, `logs`, `wooden_*`, `signs` and `fence_gates` tags, which is what makes the whole set axe-mineable and craftable the way any other wood is.
- Add **naringin** and the **CYP3A4** index:
  - Naringin is what grapefruit carries, 0..**10** - ten slices - and it is cleared over one game day. It has no effect of its own; everything it does, it does through the enzyme.
  - CYP3A4 runs 0..**100** and sits at **85** in a body that has eaten no grapefruit. Naringin is a step function on it rather than a curve, so the index only ever holds one of five values: **85** at 2 or below, **60** past 2, **45** past 4, **25** past 7, and **10** at 8.5 or above.
- Milk now counts as a drink, so drinking a bucket of it adds the standard **15 water**. In 26.3 vanilla's milk is a plain `Item` carrying a `CONSUMABLE` component rather than the `MilkBucketItem` of older versions, which is what lets the mod's `Item.finishUsingItem` hook see it at all.
- Add **grapefruit juice**: `minecraft:sugar` + one `aliment:grapefruit_slice` + a **water bottle** crafts one `aliment:grapefruit_juice`, which is the slice pressed into a bottle. It is a drink rather than a food, so it is **0 hunger** and always edible, and it takes the standard drink's **15 water** where the slice takes 5. It carries the slice's **1 naringin** and **10 vitamin C** unchanged, and adds **0.7 glucose** from the sugar - charged as bread is charged rather than as the plant food the fruit is, because sugar is the fast carbohydrate. Ten glasses is the naringin cap, exactly as ten slices is.
  - The ingredient is not `minecraft:potion` but a `fabric:components` filter requiring `minecraft:potion_contents` of `minecraft:water`, so the recipe will not accept an arbitrary brewed potion. Vanilla's `Ingredient` is a `HolderSet<Item>` and cannot express this, and a filter that fails to parse drops the recipe silently, so the self test both asks the recipe manager for the recipe by name and asserts that a water bottle matches while an awkward potion does not.
  - Its sprite is drawn in **vanilla's own potion style**, the convention the mod's other potions already follow: vanilla's `potion.png` bottle and `potion_overlay.png` liquid, with the greyscale liquid tinted to the slice's flesh so the glass reads as grapefruit. The bottle is vanilla's pixel for pixel; only the tint is ours.

releases.notes:
## 1.0.1

### Added
- Add blood glucose and the insulin index, in **mmol/L**, and the four-item diagnostic chain that reads it:
  - `glucose` and `insulin` are new `ModelState` fields. Glucose is the second quantity in the model that is *spent* rather than regulated to a set point: only food puts it back, and the fasting path runs from 5.0 to the 3.5 floor in exactly two game days, slowing down past it.
  - The reference range is **4.0 – 5.5 mmol/L**. Above **8.0** the insulin index climbs twice as steeply, so the higher the sugar the more insulin and the faster it comes down; a meal of anything from 6 to 30 mmol/L is back inside the reference range within half a game day.
  - Food raises glucose by class: **bread +0.7**, **cooked meat and fish +0.5**, **raw meat and fish +0.4**, **plant food +0.4**. Everything edible that is not meat or bread counts as plant food, so living on berries does not avoid the cost.
  - Hypoglycaemia, on the way down: **< 2.0 mining fatigue**, **< 1.7 adds weakness**, **< 1.3 adds magic damage** of `(1.3 - glucose)` every two seconds. Eight game days without food leaves a body at 0.97 mmol/L.
  - The body's own insulin is switched off at the bottom of the reference range, so it can never drive a player hypoglycaemic on its own; injected insulin aspart is not switched off by anything.
- Add `aliment:insulin_injection` (insulin aspart, +10.0 a dose, ceiling 60.0, cleared over one game day). It is the one drug in the mod that makes a body worse on purpose: one dose from a normal 5.0 is a survivable dip to about 2.7, and two are a crisis.
- Add `aliment:glucose_meter`, `aliment:glucose_test_strip`, `aliment:bloodied_test_strip` and `aliment:microneedle`:
  - Right-click with the microneedle to prick a finger, which then bleeds for **15 seconds** (300 ticks); the lancet takes a point of damage.
  - Right-click with a test strip while the finger is still bleeding and it becomes a bloodied one. A strip used after the drop has dried is refused with an action-bar hint, and the drop is spent on the strip it was caught on.
  - Hold the meter in the **main** hand and the bloodied strip in the **off** hand and right-click to print `Blood glucose: 5.1 mmol/L` in chat (`当前血糖：5.1 mmol/L` in `zh_cn`); the strip is used up.
- Add the glucose chain to the village and pillager outpost chests: the insulin injection at **10%**, and the meter, test strips (**5–9** at a time) and microneedle at **35%** each.
- Add the five item sprites, generated by the new `tools/gen_glucose_textures.ps1`.
- Add JEI (Just Enough Items) recipe viewer support for grindstone grinding/crushing recipes.
- Add wheat brewing and beer distillation pipeline:
  - Wheat (`minecraft:wheat`) can now be added into the glass fermentation tank as a fermentable substrate alternative to sugar.
  - Inoculating the tank with brewer's yeast (`aliment:brewer_yeast`) initiates fermentation, producing fermented beer mash.
  - Distilling the fermented wheat mash over a campfire through a condenser pipe into an empty cauldron produces a Beer Cauldron (`aliment:beer_cauldron`).
  - Bottling the beer cauldron with a glass bottle yields Beer (`aliment:beer`, 5% ethanol), providing hydration and mild alcoholic effect when consumed.
  - Added full visual textures and models for beer item, beer cauldron, and fermentation tank liquid states (`wheat` and `beer`).
- Add multi-tier alcohol cauldron distillation pipeline and dynamic alcohol naming:
  - 7% wine and 40% wine can now be poured into a cauldron.
  - Heating an alcohol cauldron over a lit campfire with a condenser pipe above it distills the liquid into a collection cauldron:
    - 7% wine distills through the condenser pipe into 40% wine.
    - 40% wine distills through the condenser pipe into 75% alcohol.
    - 75% alcohol can be poured back into a cauldron and distilled into 98% alcohol.
  - Dynamic naming: Items with ethanol concentration >= 70% (75% and 98%) are named "Alcohol" instead of "Wine".
